Dataset Provenance & Quality Control

Ground-truth empirical psychometric research dataset from the Open Source Psychometrics Project (Lovibond & Lovibond, 1995).

📋 DASS-42 Clinical Subscales

The Depression Anxiety Stress Scales measure 3 distinct emotional states with 42 Likert items (rescaled to standard 0-3 clinical severity):

SubscaleItems CountClinical Target CutoffSeverity Tiers
Depression (D) 14 Items (Q3, Q5, Q10...) Score ≥ 14 (Mod-to-Severe) Normal Mild Mod Extremely Severe
Anxiety (A) 14 Items (Q2, Q4, Q7...) Score ≥ 10 Autonomic arousal, situational dread
Stress (S) 14 Items (Q1, Q6, Q8...) Score ≥ 15 Nervous tension, impatience, irritability

🛡️ Automated Data Quality Control

Strict validity filtering to remove careless, bot, or automated respondents:

  • Validity Catch Words (VCL6, VCL9, VCL12): Participants endorsing fake English words were automatically excluded.
  • Age Sanity Bounds: Retained respondents between 10 and 100 years old.
  • Stratified Split: 80% Training (27,660 samples) / 20% Holdout Test (6,915 samples).
  • Ethical Privacy: Anonymized at source; 0 PII; academic research scope.

Complete Explainability Techniques Showcase (6 Methods)

Combining game-theoretic, surrogate, gradient, activation, attention, and recourse mechanisms.

1. SHAP (Shapley Values)

Game-theoretic Shapley attributions for global importance and participant-specific local breakdowns.

2. LIME (Local Surrogates)

Interpretable local linear approximations with rule condition thresholds and confidence weights.

3. Integrated Gradients

Axiomatic path integrals satisfying completeness and implementation invariance for neural classifiers.

4. Grad-CAM (1D Activation)

Localizes activation energy across psychometric subscales (Depression vs Anxiety vs Stress).

5. Attention-Based Explanations

Transformer multi-head self-attention weights mapping cross-symptom clinical couplings.

6. Counterfactual Recourse

Actionable minimal Likert score interventions to transition high-risk individuals into normal risk.

Task 3: Multimodal Explainability Engine

Synchronized fusion and attribution across 5 clinical data streams: Survey, Behavioural Latency, Text, Speech Acoustics, and Physiology.

Modality Attribution Radar

Dynamic attention gating weights showing the proportional contribution of each stream.

Modality Contribution Percentages

Ablation risk shift and feature importance within each synchronized data stream.

Task 2: Quantitative XAI Comparative Evaluation

Scientific benchmarking of Faithfulness (Deletion AUDC), Gini Sparsity, Concordance, and Execution Speed.

Inter-Explainer Concordance (Spearman ρ)

Measures the degree of rank correlation agreement between SHAP, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and Recourse.

Faithfulness Deletion Curves

Progressive masking of top attributed features. Lower curve indicates higher explanatory fidelity.
